I agree with the slide move, but there would be exceptions. If you slide and you're still in the tunnel (or for a better example, under MINES), you should be able to crawl. Examples below.

Let's say crouch is down.
o If you're standing still, you can duck/move into crawl mode by pressing and holding down. You can also crawl at a sluggish pace by holding left or right.
o If you're moving (nomatter how fast) and you press down to crouch, you will slide (head-first would make the most sense in this case) and friction will kick in at 2x (or 1.5x) as much as standing motion. You cannot gain speed from crawling until you have reached crawling speed, which afterwards you can continue crawling.
o If you slide (or crawl) into a half-square crawlspace, you cannot get up until there is room, and you let go of down. If you slide under mines, you better hold down.
o If you let go of down in the middle of a slide, N will flip out of the slide in a roll and continue running with the same momentum. If you press jump while sliding, N will flip out of the slide into a jump, still holding the same momentum.
o For vertical crawlspaces, N should also be able to tilt into one of these. Holding crouch, he can drop down one. Letting go of down while inside one will make him stick to the walls in an attempt to slow down. He cannot enter one vertically, but jumping makes him climb (not jump) slowly upwards.

Wow, I'm hoping this becomes a feature. I put alot of work into explaining this. Mare? Please show interest.

JUMPS,

#33594 12 2004-10-26T00:27:09Z TornadoTK
Or alot less coding.

1. Jump x 0.75 and Movement Speed x 0.5
2. Every time he is in water, give him 20 seconds of breathing time (which you recover when your head is out of the water, and at the same speed you lose it), and you don't even need a bar, it'd be better if you had to count or reflex it.
3. Forget that, drones shouldn't die in the water. They WILL electrify it though when they occupy a water tile that connects to another water square (in chain reaction form).
4. Same for a thwump.
5. Lasers will fire, but if N is occupying a water zone, it will not harm him (unless a body part is not in the water and touching the laser.
6. Missles hitting the water will slowly float to the bottom. When it hits N or a wall, it will explode.
7. Floor guards in water will only do good in electrifying the water for N.
8. Bounce blocks will have more resistance like you said.
9. Jump pads will have resistance as well.
10-12. Ditto.

The thing to realize here is probably one variable: "In Water". It's either 0 or 1. If N is in water, the laser won't work on him, he moves differently, and all the other effects take place. Also, water should be a tile so its easier to place it.

It would add some fun to N though. You gotta admit.

Low Gravity Mode - Less Gravity/Friction
Flipped Mode - Screen is upside down and backwards.
No Reflex Mode - Buttons take 1/4 of a second to respond at all times.
Druggie Mode - All objects are replaced with different ones (including N), and tile/background colors change in a rainbow effect. Try playing with THAT on. (Actually, it'd be fun seeing zap drones become pac-men. XD But who would N be?)
Time Flies Mode - 30 second limit for the episodes, and gold counts as +1.
Tiny Mode - Screen is 1/2 it's size.
Old School Mode - Screen is zoomed 2x on N's location, scrolling along with him like a platformer.
One Life Challenge Mode - Have the one life challenge mode implemented. 0-5th Columns, but also an All Column mode (if they dare). High scores can be implemented.
Survival Mode - Unlocks a Survival episode (avoiding enemies for as long as they can, that kind). Timer counts up from 0. High scores can be implemented.

Jump Mode - N is replaced with Ogmo from the Jump series. That'd be creepy but fun to do, just gotta get permission.
Matrix Mode - Enemies are 1/2 speed, and you can jump 2x as high.

#50620 34 2005-02-16T23:26:54Z TornadoTK
I'm not superstitious or religious in any way, unfortunately.

I believe that when you die, everything just stops working. It literally stops. End of the line. There's no fading to black, there's no soul being freed. You just stop thinking, stop noticing, stop living. I believe that the "light at the end of the tunnel" is just the feeling you get when your eyesight begins to fade to white, and the faint feeling of death (or near-death) puts you in that "floating" state of mind. I believe that ghosts in pictures are just weird light captures (if it isn't Photoshop, ). Feeling chills down your spine and thinking a ghost was looking over your shoulder. Deja Vu (even though it still scares me) is either your mind making you believe that you've seen it happen before, you have had a past experience with it, or dreamed/thought about it once by chance.

And I'm most likely wrong.

#2294 1 2005-03-24T14:42:01Z TornadoTK
In the Playstation magazines, they have an article where someone mails in a brief idea of a game (what kind, features, what makes it special, doesn't exceed three paragraphs). I figure we could do it here. Toss in your best ideas for a game, and give other people the Green Light, or tell them to go back to the drawing board. I'll start it, and someone gives me a verdict, and starts a new game idea for the next player to judge.

Game: "Enemy Terroritory"

You're a spy that got himself put into Desert Storm. Unfortunately, you're mission was to assassinate the general and leave, but with as many soldiers as there are, you're gonna have to kill people off one by one to get out of there alive. Oh, and don't let anyone see you doing so, or you'll be shot on sight (like your own personal firing squad).

ET will be a FPS with a lot of Commandos-like gameplay. You'll be making and breaking bonds with the soldiers you work with. One area of the game will be at the base camp, where you can wander around (or kill when you see an opportunity), and talk to people to find out the latest gossip (if they know theres a spy afoot, they'll be alot more alert, so you'll think twice about killing anytime soon). You can sleep, which takes you to the next area of play: The battlefield. You'll be sent out on missions with your team, and you must find ways to kill them. They can die in battle, you can kill them, or you can leave them alive to wait for another mission. Whatever you do, don't let them think you're intentionally doing so. They will radio in if they get the chance to.

The special thing about my idea: Realism. No crosshairs (cept for the ones on your guns), no run meters, no reloading leftover bullets into your current clip (wasting two shots and reloading will waste a LOT of ammo). This game will be realistic in gameplay to intensify the action.

Like it?
#55861 13 2005-03-25T04:02:12Z TornadoTK
@brickman: Well, I did have this down, I just didn't add it in. The guy will want to survive, and so will you. You are allowed to kill the General at any moment. If you go overboard and people don't trust you (since you can bond with the soldiers), you'll be interrogated, or even executed by a one who is afraid of you. Pretty much, your goal is to get out alive. It's somewhat like a Freedom Fighters storyline; What if a spy infiltrated our Desert Storm troops and killed them all?

#57074 44 2005-03-30T04:17:50Z TornadoTK
Maniac, your idea sounds alright, but it's just about GTA minus the violence and fun things to do. List some things besides missions that you do after you finish the main game. Please include shopping cart racing/stunts.



As for my game, it was a simple RPG battle game that played somewhat like the PSX game Battle Hunter. Each player was dealt five cards out of a 52 card deck. The suit of the card was the card type, and the number was the card value.

Hearts = Defense (Damage that can be taken)
Spades = Attack (Damage dealt)
Diamonds = Movement (Move yourself)
Clubs = Movement+ (Move yourself or an enemy)

2 through King = 2 through 13
Ace = MAX

You placed your pieces on the boards (8x16 squares). After everyone places their piece (and are happy with positioning), the game starts. The first player either uses a card and draws another, drops their cards for new cards, moves one space, or waits. You cannot move diagonally. When you move next to a player (or move one next to you), you can attack. They must be adjecent to you, not diagonal from you. You pick a spade to attack with, and they pick a heart to defend with. If the attacker's card is higher, the defender's maximum card hold is reduced by one. When a player loses his last card, he dies. If the defenders card is higher, nothing happens. Both players discard the cards they used in battle and draw new ones. Aces are the MAX cards, which is the highest card in battle, and can place you anywhere in movement. Last man standing wins.

A little complicated, but fun when you get 8 people playing, and theres a moshpit battlefield in the center of the stage.

Base Weapons
Polar Star
Fireball
Bubbler
Missles
Blade

Swap Weapons
Polar Star for Machine Gun
Polar Star and Fireball for Snake
Missles for Missles V2
Blade for Nemesis
Polar Star for Spur

#71172 66 2005-05-31T04:16:21Z TornadoTK
Actually, you can set it up like so.

Both players CAN cross sides, but what good would that do? So don't, though you can.
If the ball lands on the net and stays, its still in game, and you could jump and hit it still.
Tons of rules permitting what can and can't go down.
Hitting the ball at certain velocities and angles changes its trajectory and speed.
Obstacles, enemies, and mines CAN be activated if you wish.
The net should bounce the ball back only at the top, the bottom lets the ball go and counts as a fault.
If items are to be placed by the opponents, it can only be UNDER the tile net range.
Ninjas start on their side, against the middle of the side walls, to prevent early death.
The ball spawns on top of the net for a serve and for posession; First to touch it gets the first ball to be their serve for that serve.
For each serve after the first, the ball is placed in the center of the servers box, in the tile net area, and held there until it's hit.

Crazy rules to understand, but you just gotta piece my brain together, and right now it hurts. Picture of my arena coming soon.

#78993 12 2005-06-27T18:24:48Z TornadoTK
ROM and Emulator Q&A:

"Is it legal if you own the cartridge but it's broken?"
Yes. That's why we have Backup ROM's. If you got a broken cartridge for a cookie, you now own that game. Selling the system and keeping the games is still legal for owning those ROM's.

"They should stick IP-tracking & time-counting files onto ROMs or somethin'."
They can't really do that to ALL Roms. Backup files belong to the person that created it. Nobody else. You can't just say, "Hey! That's our game you're trying to play! Stop that, and use the broken cartridge in your garage! It's under your car's front left tire. -Signed, Sonic Team". They could publish their own files, but why do that? There are too many sites online anyway.

Unfortunately most N64 games blow.
Excluding Mario 64, SSB, Goldeneye, the Mario Party games, and the Zelda games.

#79897 26 2005-06-30T10:04:09Z TornadoTK
Sporks
In the modern day society, our demand for greater tools increases rapidly. Computers have gotten much faster, cars have gotten more efficient, and it even comes down to the household eating utensil. Normally, food would require you to use a fork and a spoon seperately- can't eat that tomato soup with a fork, nor eat chicken with a spoon. Until the 1990's, we were plagued with this overworking of the kitchen... But look no further, because the spork is the solution to all our problems.

Sporks are basically spoons that have a forks prongs at the end of the round end. Eating soup? Go ahead. How about a baked potato? Go for it! Using amazing 20th Century technology, the Spork allows us to get rid of our spoons and forks, and eliminate the factor of having the wrong utensil for the wrong food.

Unfortunately enough, Sporks are overlooked in most cases. Like the hybrid car, Sporks are known to be not needed in the common home, because we've already got spoons and forks. By using Sporks, we cut down silverware maitenance time by fifty percent instantly. Also, the fact that knives come into play makes the Spork revolution look bad. We can't have knives on the handle, or we'd cut ourselves! Luckily, we've got 40 of the world's top scientists locked up, working on the solution.

But what about the spoons and forks you have at home? If you indeed buy Sporks, what will you do with your old kitchenware? Nobody will buy it with Sporks on the market! Well, it's simple. Spoons can be used as catapult prototypes for a science project, and balance well on the noses of many. Forks can be used as darts, deadly weapons, and a lighter version of an airhorn when scratched against a plate. There are choices a plenty when you wish to put your old utensils to good use, and if you can't find one, mold the steel into a statue! It's fun for the whole family!

With the upcoming Spork craze, you may want to invest in Sporks. They may be worth very little now, but when they become in demand, you can expect Sporks to sell for over $20,000 a pop! Talk about income! Don't get left behind, get a jump start to the future! Buy Sporks today!

#84267 33 2005-07-17T18:21:11Z TornadoTK
Messageboard Games Dying

We here at Metanet Incorperated take notice to the recent number of Messageboard Games that are dying. I, for one, was responsible for this beautiful game to be pushed closer and closer to the great beyond known as Page 2. My actions were unintentional, of course, but why did it happen? Did I forget it existed? No. Did I not want to post? No. These games are becoming extinct because of people like me, who rarely check on posts that have come to a "halt". I quote one of our executive employees, Mr. Chimney Sweep; "I'll wait 24 hours, and if not much has happened since then the 'chosen one' shall be picked." After this remark, he waited four days (he was off by 72 hours!) until he posted, leaving my mind to be covered in the dust of anticipation. But just how do we make sure that these games don't die? What would this world become without the Game Naming Game? How could we survive without the Removal Game? We must find out why people begin to drift.

Many games that are created to be Messageboard Games don't find much appeal by the members (see "A Story..." and "Name That Video"), so they instantly drift to the bottom. To prevent this, we should think if people would like it or not, not just us. Also, keeping games alive is an issue, and I see two reasons. First of all, some games come to a halt when nobody can add on to certain things (see "I am the king", "Game Naming Game" and "Guess the Quote in Poly's Sig Game!"). Posters wish to stump the other members, and because of this, the game is destroyed. Don't stump the forum, just give them a challenge. Secondly, people forget that it's their turn (see "Game Naming Game" and this topic). To correct this, we should PM Bomb the person that's up next. That way, they can't receive any more PM's unless they haul their ass over here.

This situation demands urgent attention, and I ask all of you to deliver it, for the sake of our loving Messageboard Games.

Signed, TornadoTK - Unofficial Mod of the Game Naming Game

#92915 231 2005-08-21T08:37:47Z TornadoTK
I suck at speed. I'm pretty decent at being cautious, survival, and commiting to things. By the way, I've been trying this ever since I got the 0th Column high score, and take out a week and a half (I forgot about it in a rush of real life). I'd say about 30-50 tries every day I've gave it a go. It's not that hard.

Learn the levels you tend to mess up on, practice it until you know the run in and out, and you can do it at least 10 times in a row. Don't be speedy, that leads to death. Learn a safe run that prevents death in as many cases as possible. In 0th Column especially, there are a LOT of episodes where gold has no value since you have all the time you need.

Then, complete the episode your level is in twice without dying. It's a good practice. After you can do that (for all the levels you have problems with), go for it. And remember, slow and steady remains sane as he plays. I mean, wins the race, of course. Heh heh...

EDIT: I guess my N skill is now consistency. I wouldn't doubt seeing LittleViking or even you, nevermore, pulling off an even greater 0th Column score. Hell, I say go for it. I need a reason to come back to 0th.

EDIT2: Oh, and I've got about 3 more runs at this, and I'm gonna say screw it and go to bed. If something comes up, I'll post it.

Maple Story is just like you said, hack-and-slash, but partying up makes the game a little better. Quests are normally "Kill X to Get Y" but can lead to "Complete This Platforming-Action Hair-Ripping Puzzle-Maze" and back randomly. It's all in the taste of the game.

Another freeware game in development is an MMORPG called Flyff. It's not complete yet, but so far, it's kinda like a mini-World of Warcraft. You got a basic starting character, choose class at level 15, learn combos and level them up, armor/weapons have durability (though they wear down slow). Unfortunately, you might not have too much fun if you dont dig the basic Kill X Get Y quests, or even Deliver X Get Y quests. But if you got a friend in the game, it's a real charm to play. I'm a level 15 or 16 Assist (Helper-Spell Class), and I go around giving people heals and such (to train my spells, XD). But its definately worth a shot. Oh, and at level 20, you can get a hoverboard. Woo.

As for Tibia, I gotta agree. It sucks biiiiig time. I'd rather play Goonzu or Rose Online... Sheesh...

#104043 4 2005-09-27T07:14:14Z TornadoTK
Glad to see someone checked it out.

You earn a LOT more bounty past level 10. Just look for Bonuses as you play. I don't think I'm accurate, but..

Blue = Clean kills. Either accuracy, combo, or damage taken.
Purple = Double kill or large damage.
Gold = Chain two kills in one combo.
Red = Headshot (Head hitbox is actually the neck)

Also, don't be afraid to get cheesy. Use the rifle to killsteal in the mansion corridor, dagger-stun the people you know can't safe fall out of it and blast them on the floor, and when in doubt, get some HP/AP. As for items, learn your strategy while playing.

Pistol - Long-to-Medium range, less accuracy required.
Revolver - Medium Range, more accuracy required.
Shotgun - Only for close range players, or koreans.
SMG's - No accuracy? Get close and spray away.
Rifle - Accurate, and somewhat strong. Great in corridors.
Rockets - Only strong when used on multiple enemies at once.
MG's - Haven't reached level 25 yet.

Frag: Useful in close-quarters and smoking your enemy out.
Flash: Use only during getaways, or to confuse moshpit gunners.
Smoke: ...I don't see what this does. Ever.
HP Repair: Great boost of HP in Team games.
AP Repair: Almost as useful, but HP always comes first.

Learn the game, learn the weaknesses.

#4557 1 2005-09-29T06:58:39Z TornadoTK
Just got done with the first chapter of this story I'm writing. Opinions, grammar/punctuation/spelling errors, comments, and any positive feedback is appreciated. Hope you dig it.


It was a day like any other. Joe ran his fingers back through his hair and looked up. "Ah, the sun's gonna set soon," he muttered, "Better get home." The sky glowed with warm, soothing colors that seemed to fade with every step he took. As he made his way through the park, he couldn't help but notice all the parents flying kites with their children, laughing and running together. He had a kid of his own, David, who was having his second birthday in a week. Joe stopped to picture the thought of his son and himself, flying kites in the park at sunset, and resumed walking with a smile.

He walked towards the park bathroom, looking for paper towels to blow his nose. As he reached for the door, he noticed a peculiar looking man. Black suit, red tie, and his black hair slicked back and gelled, his appearance was as sharp as a pin. He looked like he could put Donald Trump into bankrupcy. He had eyes that were as golden as the buttons on his shirt, and they seemed to be fixed upon him. Strangely enough, nobody even took a glance at him, no matter how bad he stuck out. It was almost as if Joe was the only one meant to see him, like some kind of ghost. He shrugged it off and entered the bathroom.

The bathroom was filled with the stench of urine. He shrugged off the smell, walked to the paper towel dispenser and pulled down on the handle; it wouldn't budge. He moved to the toilet stalls to get some tissue paper instead, and as the door into the bathroom was out of view, he heard it open. He faltered instinctively, but he regained his composure in a heartbeat. Opening the stall, he pulled some tissue from the roll. Suddenly, he froze.

He sensed someone was behind him. In his mind, the image of the dressed-up man just wouldn't go away. That moment lasted a lifetime. Endless amounts of waiting, thinking, hoping; Hoping that nobody would be there when he turned his head. He wished that he was just imagining all of this, some kind of strange temporary paranoia. He would leave, go home to his wife and son, and continue his life as a normal citizen, as a normal, working man. He couldn't have done anything to deserve such a fate in the first place, right? His lifetime had became a moment once again, and the next thing he thought would be his last. "What is that?!?"

The sharp, cold, razor-thin wire touched his neck, giving him a feeling of death; so cold, so hidden, it made his eyes grow wide with fear. Within an instant, that cold, sharp feeling became painful and warm. He knew now, he knew what was going on, and realized why it was happening. Taking money from under his boss's nose, blackmailing his fellow employees, taking the company name and using it as a cover for his drug dealing; Every last crime, every last sin, it all began to heat the thin wire until it felt like a thread of molten steel, burning a line across his neck, through his throat. It was almost as though as this was brought onto him from Satan himself, and this man, this assassin, was the messenger. He was suffering for trying to have it all, but in the end, it would all be taken from him.

It couldn't have been a second later when he felt the blood spraying from his neck. Most of it sprayed across the walls of the bathroom stall, as the rest poured into the slice in his throat, seeping into his lungs. It was clearly over from there. The man pulls two thin, steel rods from his inner shirt pocket and stabs them into the wall above the toilet seat, leaving them a few inches apart. Placing the neck of the corpse between the spikes, he sets another rod upon the two and leaves it to support the corpse in a sitting position in the stall. Opening the stall door, he whips out a small, red handkerchief and makes quick work of any noticable stains and smears of blood. After the area is left spotless, he pockets it once again and leaves, shutting the stall and bathroom doors behind him.

As he walks away from the bathroom stall, he tilts his head back and looks to the sky with a face of remorse. It glares back at him with a deep shade of orange, as if that was an ominous message for him- A message of rejection. Looking onward, he begins walking the path out of the park, along with the few remaining people that are through with watching the setting sun. To them, it was a beautiful sight. To him, it did nothing more than remind him of who he was.

A murderer.


First Edit: Atilla

#4743 1 2005-10-13T05:10:26Z TornadoTK
DISCLAIMER: This topic will have nothing to do with actual piracy, or the act of pirating games, movies, or any media. It will only have to do with the ethics and economical effects of piracy. You have been warned.

Most people don't give two cents about the piracy issue, yet sometimes people overlook certain details. Piracy doesn't always lose money, and here is my case. I have pirated time and time again, though I cause no harm to the economy of the gaming industry, music industry, or movie industry. Why? Because 99.99999% of the time, I cannot buy that product anyway. I'm stuck out of buying anything online, and I have almost no budget to buy anything with. I'd never steal, as that takes away a physical object from another person, leaving them no choice but to not buy it, while piracy is making a copy that wouldn't make a difference if it existed or not. Now, if a company was to make no gain or loss from my act of piracy, aside from the gain of a user/fan, is it okay?

Basketball, influenced by Nanaca Crash:
Set an angle, set your power (see the game on how it should be set), and a drone smashes N in that angle/power. Nolympics, influenced by many games:
N Hyper Dash > N Hurdles > N Long Jump > N High Jump > N Wall Jump
Hyper Dash: Left and Right repetitavely to run as fast as you can.
Hurdles: Like HD with hurdles to jump over. Jump to jump. Hurdles vary in size, so hold jump to long jump.
N Long Jump: Like HD, and you jump as far as you can, while still mashing L and R to maintain your speed in mid-air.
N High Jump: Like HD, but after crossing a line, hold shift to jump at a set angle into a triangle block, then jump off of that into the air.
N Wall Jump: Like the high jump, but theres a kick off of the wall before the distance measurement (in the opposite direction of course).

Not to mention ping, the other person's lag, and so on. This has been suggested millions and billions of times, and I suggest you search the forums for a little while just to see what I mean. You should also do that before you register, since it will help you with the registration process.
6. - If you mean online 1v1, refer to the above post. If you mean a leaderboard, we have "Most Time Remaining", since that's the normal Highscore list. "Quickest One Done" is one I've personally suggested, and it never made it. The others just sound like a waste of a leaderboard, and besides, our Highscore server is taking a massive beating as we speak. We'd need more servers for this.
7. - Once again, search. Powerups ruin the simplicity of N. Sure, they might be fun, and they might have some good uses, but it's just not N. Picture 500 levels without a powerup, and then another 10 episodes with them. It just won't work. Also, I love Teh Dude's explanation on this as well. It'd ruin the balance of the game, and make the learning curve steeper than it should be.

As for the lag debate, Teh Dude has it right. Lag is just a delay, no matter what you use it in. You could say people are lagging behind, or you experienced jet lag on a plane. There is always lag in a video game, it's just that usually its not noticable. The flaw with the internet is that it isn't an instant send and receive system.
#119712 11 2005-12-02T04:55:48Z TornadoTK
Quote: mr_fsu_guy, Dec 1 2005, 06:38 AM
In online gameplay you dont send packets of every pixel that you go to. The server acts as the master server, and you send a packet saying im here in relation to the server world, the server sends it back to you and says yah thats where you are and your computer displays it. Online lag is where the server world and your world don't match up and it "lags" you forward or backward depending on where the server says you need to be. You don't have to send physics of where I'm moving where I'm going to each other. Its just a packet saying im on block 'a' in the server world, now show me that on my computer. It wouldn't be hard to display 2 N's doing their thing on 1 screen when there is no physics that need to be calculated. Its just simply where you are in relation to the server world. And trust me, if you can get Quake, and all those other games to send packets of weapons on X,Y,Z axis coordinates, thats right that is called 3d, then you can certainly send a packet to display a figure on strictly the X & Y axis.

Thanks and have a nice day.

To spoil your theory on packets:

You're saying that when I load a game at 60 frames per second, and I'm playing 15 other players running the game at 60 frames per second, then the server is sending out 3,600 packets per second?!?!?

..Wow. Anyway. Packets are NOT just XYZ coordinates for players. That's plain obvious. This is myself winging an explanation that makes sense:

Packets contain the XYZ coordinates, yes. But it's EVERYONE'S XYZ coordinates. And all of the objects. Which means all of the objects need to be constantly sent and synced. Then, packets are also.. GASP! Physics! They tell you how fast a player is going in what direction, so it can lead that player off and have to send less packets! When it doesn't do that, you begin to see the players freezing and teleporting. When packets lead off, you see the players walking forward into walls, THEN teleporting. Just like in the explanation for Quake!

Don't hate me if I'm wrong, as I said, I winged that whole thing. I know just about nothing when it comes to this, but it makes a lot of sense, and in some cases it's true.

Why I like Macs:

Why I dislike Macs:
- The game selection. Dear god, if you could make any less high quality games for the Mac, you might as well call the poor machine an N-Gage. Me and my friends are still looking for games that run well on the eMac with Network Play. Macaddict, help me out here!
- Strict model-by-model selection. With Windows, I can choose between HP, Dell, Gateway, eMachines (Why God? Why?), Alienware, and so on. I can choose my processor, my hard drive, my ram, my video card, my setup, all at a respectable price. With Mac, there's the iMac, the eMac, the G5, and other steps on the Mac ladder, with very little customization, unless you wanna get in deep.
- Ever have someone try to talk you through something you know all about already? That's what it feels like when I transition from Windows to Mac. Baby steps. Everything is just easy'ed out for me, with smooth transitions from window to window, a dock, and keyboard commands for everything. I'm used to being able to blaze on through my computer. Hell, I can open "C:\Program Files\Steam\SteamApps\tornadotk\Counter-Strike Source\cstrike\screenshots\de_dust20109.jpg" in 8 seconds- casually. Or, I can use the shortcut on my desktop to get there in two clicks. On a Mac, I feel like I'm being guided there, with beautiful scrolling and sliding transitions. There's probably an option to change this, but Windows does this automatically.
- The fanboys. The Mac community (no offense Macaddict) is full of people who wouldn't dare wait a millisecond to say that Mac > All. A lot of the bunch annoy the heck out of me.

#145611 17 2006-02-19T06:33:33Z TornadoTK
Trojans don't have to wait for a specific date, actually. Trojans generalize as maliciously-coded programs that are normally installed without permission (and more likely to be installed without any knowledge of it happening). They can be set so they boot at any set event. This can be from the moment the program is executed, or when your system clock hits 3:19:25 PM on St. Patrick's Day.

As for why it's called the Trojan and how it relates to my own definition, the Trojan Horse was brought in without knowledge of the dangers inside. The Trojans could have attacked whenever they felt like it, but waited until it was safe to ambush. Just like a trojan can attack on execution, or wait until a specific moment or instruction.

If I'm wrong, eh, so what. I think that's the perfect explanation of a trojan.

C-Stick is my deadliest weapon. Here's a tip you should learn. C-Sticking in the air is an automatic Air Attack (Can somebody say Mario's Forward+A spike move?), and you can charge normal C-Sticks (Smash Attacks) by pressing the C-Stick, then hold Z before the attack. Release Z to Smash.

@Maniac: It's really easy to kill them off. If you want to use a character you love, here's my battle strategy: Begin fighting the hand that waits on the other hand to begin a team attack. It'll stay there with sparkles nearby, waiting to get the crap kicked out of it. To fight, single jump and attack, over and over again, so you can use the second and third jumps for evasions. Also, if there's an attack that hits you often, like the grab or the walking fingers, use the Air Dodge. Kill one, kill two, it's done. You should see the NEXT Event Match, #51. Cheese Pillows

Two slices of Bread
Two slices of American Cheese
Toaster that only toasts on one side at a time
Microwave
Knife

Take two slices of bread, and put them into a one-sided toaster, only toasting one side of each slice until it's slightly crunchy.
Put two slices of American cheese in between the soft sides of the bread, and place in the microwave until it melts.
Cut the crust and some of the bread (almost one inch on all sides) off. Pinch the sides and corners closed.

You now have a cheesy pillow. But please, do NOT try to sleep on it, no matter how much you have an urge to. It gets messy.

I haven't read anything besides the first post, but here goes.

We technically do have free will. If there is something we wanna do, we'll try it. We do have the free will to go out and rob banks, rape, murder, commit genocide on Christians- whatever. There are consequences, but that does not hold you back from attempting it in the first place. Random events will happen occasionally, lets say for example, a drink driver hitting you while walking home. As random as it may seem, YOU chose to walk home, even though there is a possibility of that random event happening. Not only was it partially your fault, but you willfully took that path and went up against those "random event odds", and they happened to kick in on you. Not to mention that depending on how fit you may have been keeping yourself (I know it sounds silly), you may or may not die.

Everyone has free will, but people who do believe this don't see the odds of these random events happening that are the consequences of free will. Do what you want to do, but don't put yourself against massive odds (like my first, more criminalized example).

Do I sound like a raving idiot? I think I sound like a raving idiot.

Personally, I don't find it to be a bad game. I'm currently on Chapter 9, and it's turning out to be good storywise, and playable in gameplay. I do admit, the gameplay gets boring, and the graffiti helps nothing, but everything feeds the storyline, and at times, you can't help but play just to see what happens.

**SPOILERS, BIG SPOILERS**
Trane (the main character) starts with aspirations of being a big-time artist, but then is inspired to send a message to the police force of the future (think cops mixed with steroids and mech armor) by disobeying every graffiti-related law possible. Tagging untaggable trains, nailing spot after spot, and gaining street cred. Unfortunately, he's set up every which way, his dad was was killed for knowing trash about the mayor, and his brother (also being targeted) may be next, since Trane makes the mistake of telling someone where his hideout was. The police want Trane dead, and Trane's crew doesn't want to die, so right now, he stands alone. More story coming soon!

I still think it's worth a full playthrough rental.

#176577 9 2006-05-16T09:21:32Z TornadoTK
I'm not Mare, nor Raigan, but I can help answer your questions.

How do you guys get into doing this?
Simple. You just stick with an idea, learn what you need to learn, and adapt from there. It'll take some time, though, so be patient.

At what age?
Any age can really start making a game. It might take age to comprehend the concepts of making one, but you can start the process whenever you feel like it.

Does it cost?
It depends on what you use to create the game, because the foundation is everything. As said before, Flash is expensive, but effective. There's always C++, or for starters, Game Maker. You can do it without any cost, but then again, you'll have to sacrifice more time or more quality.

Is it really, really worth it?
Freeware games (assuming you're making freeware) are never worth it if you're doing it for the money. If it's for the fans, you will get that feeling of pride when you release a game that people really dig.

Just remember, it's not always the cake you'd imagine it to be. If you need help brainstorming ideas, idea-checking (what's good/bad/improvable), beta testing, or spreading word about it, drop me a PM, or reach my AIM/MSN.

Nah, I actually did it with a god tower. Accurately shoot off all your corner boxes with revolver shots that rebound once (or twice if you want more points), then move all of the dead boxes to the middle of the field, and arrange them in a line. Get to the opposite side of where you want to go, run into the boxes, and while running, start to fly. Chances are this wont work on the first try, but eventually, youll carry all of the boxes and create a tower. Now just whack the red box with a dead one and youre done!

DS Lite Differences:
Rounder buttons that stick out more.
Size is definately smaller.
Shape is more.. Jewelry box-like.
Power button is now an "out of the way' switch.
Backlight can now be changed with a button instead of at the DS Menu.

Stylus is thicker and heavier.

Another one of mine is an FPS loosely based off of Smash Bros. Everyone starts out in some kind of floating arena. #10759 1 2006-08-21T07:04:39Z TornadoTK
Now before you get offended, this whole discussion will be based on theory.

I got in trouble for using the word "gay" negatively in English a while back. My justification for using it was this:

The way I used the word "gay", it would make the most sense to replace it with the word "unjust". Then again, people use words like "stupid", "queer", "retarded", "crazy", and the like, all as negative adjectives. When you really piece it together, you aren't really downsizing homosexuality. Sure, they may feel this way, but that's because they're offended for personal reasons. Anyway. When you call something or someone retarded, do you really intend for that person to believe that they're retarded? Of course not. It's a figure of speech. So you meant to make a gesture at their intelligence, right? Now, of course this would supposedly attach a negative meaning to it, but doesn't who you're talking to matter?

Let's say you call a retarded person "retarded" (excuse my non-politically-correctness, but if that word offends you, or any word I say, you can refer to me in a PM), aren't you just stating a fact? Now calling a mentally-stable person retarded is, of course, a lie. But why would you say that? BECAUSE ITS A JOKE. I will call you retarded, but it's not like being retarded is some horrible group of people that you don't want to be a part of. It's just that the person you're referring to does not want to be a part of that group.

Let's stick that idea back into my original example. I call a straight man gay. Why? Because its a joke. Not because being gay is a bad thing, because the man I'm referring to is straight, and usually will not WANT to be gay, which is therefore an insult. If I called him Black, yet he is White, it doesn't come off to be so much of an insult anymore, right? Because, he doesn't mind being a different race. It doesn't bother him as much. But when you call him gay, it's an insult? Why?

If you call a guy a woman, it's an insult. If you call a racist white man a black man, it's an insult. If you call a Catholic a Jew, oh yeah, that's an insult. Not that being Black, Female, or Jewish is bad! It's just that those people would not want to be called those specific things!

Now when you take this on less specific nouns, such as a game. "This game is gay" assumes that the game takes on the average person most people would dream up. "White male, straight, Catholic, somewhat intelligent". This may vary between areas, but then again, America is where this issue is hot. Now, if you give any item human traits such as those five key traits, the average result is that some form of "stupid", "girly" and "gay" are going to be the key negative comments, while "evil", "the devil", and "Insert Minority Here" are definately said less.

Now, I have a few gay friends, and I do joke around with them. They understand my point of view, or just don't care, thanks to the "Sticks and Stones" quote. But they're already homosexual, right? It isn't funny unless I'm somewhat attacking a persons comfort zone. So what could I be saying?

I call them hetero's.

Then again when you break it down into stereotypes, you get Rednecks, Pretty Kids, Nerds, Stoners, Skaters, etc. Stereotyping makes groups of people easier to identify, but don't automatically judge using the stereotyping system. That's how the system gets ruined.

Also, that's how words get ruined. Slang makes things easier to say, and offers more ways to say it. I don't want to have to say "That's something that I dislike" instead of "That's gay/stupid/retarded/garbage/poor/dumb/bullshit/crappy". I mean, think of the word "bitch". Female dog! It's offensive to be called a female dog? If someone calls you a bitch, you don't think of a female dog. You don't even think of the meaning of the word, right? You just don't want to be called that.

That's where I get my point on why words turn into bad names. You don't want to be stupid. You don't want to be retarded. You don't want to be a devil. And in most cases (not saying all, I'm again referring to that picture of the straight white guy), you don't want to be gay. When you're called something you don't want to be, that's an insult. Society just doesn't think like that anymore. Back when we were kids, you'd call someone a stupid-face, and they'd cry. Why? Well, because when you're a kid, you don't care what a stupid-face is, but you know you don't want to be one by instinct alone.

#11995 1 2006-10-29T20:00:49Z TornadoTK
I'm thinking about pitching an idea for a racing game. No idea for a name, story, or anything; this is strictly my idea for gameplay mechanics so far.

The game plays like a cross between Midnight Club 2, and Need for Speed: Most Wanted. The game is divided into two parts, which are Free Roam and Driving. In Free Roam, you're free to drive around without a goal. You can drive to upgrade shops (upgrade your car), detail shops (make it look pretty), car dealerships (lost your car?), raceways (make some side-cash) and garages (your own, or your team's). The new use for free-roam, however, is to discover the city.

Your map will begin blank from the beginning of the game. With every street you drive on (or near, but that's only a few feet), it will uncover it for you on the map. As you drive around, you uncover more and more of the map. Secret paths such as alleyways, boarded/gated areas, and general paths that you can drive once you see them are unlocked only through driving them, and are a darker shade on your map. Stunt paths, buildings, and other major shortcut areas that are not meant to be driven on cannot be automapped. Instead, you can drop down Point of Interest (POI) markers on your map.

POI markers can be simple shapes, like dots or lines. You can also shape circles, squares, and freeform triangles over the area you want. Then you can name your area, and take a snapshot of the area from the point you marked. See a parking garage you can jump out of? POI it with a dot. Does driving through the stadium shave seconds off of your time? POI it with a line. Does the broken freeway wall lead to a straightaway below? POI it with a triangle arrow.

But why bother with POI's when you have a map? During the Driving section, you'll be given one of three racing situations: A-to-B gives you a start, and an end. This is the majority of what you'll be racing, so knowing the city gives you the advantage. Circuit will be used from time to time, and hitting shortcut after shortcut is a key to success. Evasion is an event that can happen in or out of a racing event. Police will be around, and driving off-road, hitting cars, buildings, or any object for that matter will get them onto you. Running a red light is enough for you to get tailed by a cop. You want them off of your tail, and there's only one way to do it - you have to shake 'em. Alleyways, jumps, buildings, and anything you can drive into and drive out of will be your only hope, because driving on city streets with the cops behind you is like running from a train in a tunnel. Use your POI's to ditch the 5-0.

TACK 1 - I'm definitely not throwing in any collector missions (ex. 100 secret packages, 30 stunt jumps, etc.) because it's pointless to drive around and try to collect things for a 100% rating.

TACK 2 - For stunts, there will be a button to start a recording of a demo, and when you finish it, it saves a rough copy of what you made for a showcase edit mode where you edit the clip you created with fancy camera angles.

TACK 3 - Thanks to Zres for the inspiration for a storyline idea.
--------------------------------
"Money. Respect. Pride. You had it all until Edgar rolled into town. Word on the street spread that the new guy from Riverman's Falls was talking trash about taking down Graystown's best racer. He's beaten a few of the lower tier, but you challenged him anyway, and put your garage on the line. So much that did for you, because he smoked you with a run you've never seen before. With that, you lose your garage, your fame, and everything you worked for.

But now is your time to strike back. Your boy Redd heard that Edgar is bringing his crew in to take your cars back to Riverman's Falls, and he's bringing the title of Graystown's champ with him. You're going to his city to return the favor and win back what's yours..

..and his."
--------------------------------

TACK 4 - The racing section of the game will include a checkpoint system created entirely by you. Before each race, you set down your own checkpoints that show you your own driving run. They are not necessary to succeed, but if you want to be reminded of which turns you wanted to make, you can drop them down in order. An arrow will point to your next checkpoint, and if you miss a checkpoint, there will be a button to skip to the next one.


That's just the main part of the game, I got too lazy to type the rest. How does it sound? I always thought finding shortcuts was overlooked in racing games, so I wanted the player to learn the shortcuts beforehand.

Throw in ideas, suggestions, pro's/con's, or even storylines, or a title for the game itself. I may just submit it to Rockstar. God forbid I let EA get their hands on it.

#250165 9 2006-11-05T01:39:11Z TornadoTK
For anyone who doesn't play DDR, here's what the modifiers mentioned mean:

Boost: Arrows start slower than usual, then speed up as they move up the screen.
Dark: Target arrows (gray arrow markers at the top) disappear.
Hidden: Arrows disappear halfway up the screen.
2x: Arrows move 2x as fast up the screen.
Reverse: Arrows move from top to bottom.

Now, as for your scores, all of them are basically the same as playing on Heavy. 2x, Boost, and Dark don't constitute skill, since they give little change to the song. Hidden and Reverse only take more reading skill, which can be demonstrated on a controller as well.

Paranoia Eternal - Good song, stream-y. Good work on it.
I Feel.. - Very odd beat for this song. Also a bit hard. Good work.
A Stupid Barber - This songs just easy.
Wild Rush - Again, pretty easy. Slow paced, as well.
Tsugaru - Stamina run until the end, but I can A it, and I'm way out of shape.
Jet World - Streamed song, but there are parts that are tricky if you're new to it.
Ecstacy - Easy song. It's like playing Standard.
.59 - This one's also a stamina song, but the whole way through.

Not trying to dumb you down, since you are good (about my level actually), but there are always better players. =P

Since we're on the topic, what are your bests for these songs? (on Heavy, naturally):
The Legend of MaxX
Trip Machine Survivor
Drop Out
Paranoia Eternal
Paranoia Dirty Mix

#250209 23 2006-11-05T03:02:11Z TornadoTK
"Well I could tell you that if it was released on PS2, PSP, XBOX, or PC I would be buying it immediatly! It sounds great. "

More realistically, this would launch on a next-gen console. You know, since it's not in development, and all.


"I was just wondering that when you put down your own check points in a race... How would know where to put them? Like would you be looking at a map to put them or do you do like a test drive and drive around till you find the fastest route and then put them in where you think you will need them?"

You put the checkpoints wherever you feel. In A-to-B races, your only goal is to make it to point B as fast as you can. If you have a Muscle car, I'm sure you'd want to head for the freeway, or any straightaways, since that's where you do your best. If your speed isn't too great, but that shorter, windy road is perfect for a car with better handling, you can take that road instead. Checkpoints are unnecessary markers that let you mark a path before a race starts, so you never get lost. A map will open up right before a race, and you can place down checkpoints as you please. You can place checkpoints in areas that you don't know about, but what good will that do you? If you fail a race, however, you can always prepare better for the second go. It's like mapping a route in real life, except for the fact that you can't have a huge arrow float over your car.


"I thought that if you were to put in check points for a race there should be a set number of check points that you could put in this would vary depending on how long the race was and how far though the game it was."

Well, some people want many points, and some would use very few, so there will just be a set limit. That way, you can use as many as you want. How you race is your decision.

I have Quasar, and it's actually pretty easy. If you want harder songs, look for BeMaNiRuLeR's G2 and MaxX Eternity. Then there's Ensyther's Tears Are Forever, and Quickening.

I can mash a good StepMania, and I recommend it for people who want to get better at DDR itself. It trains your eye to see more complex patterns without the need to use as much physical activity. Eventually, if you play OHTF (one hand, two fingers), you'll notice that your fingers relate to the position of your feet on the real pad, and when you get on DDR again, voila! You're suddenly better. Just build physical stamina, and maybe some crazy legs, and you can easily nail the highest 9 Foot songs.

#251095 13 2006-11-07T05:29:47Z TornadoTK
I think that my most favored gaming moment would have to be in Counter Strike: Source. Normally, I could care less about this game, but this was just the marvel of the day.

Map of de_dust2

Game is 6 on 5, in the Counter-Terrorist's favor. I'm on the Terrorist team, and my whole team goes down to Bombsite A, while I go up towards B. In the previous rounds, we we're doing that same plan they've been doing, so I feel like not dying with my team for once. My whole team gets wiped and drops the bomb. 6v1.

I look out the door from B to A, and it's clear. I run out, and a mob of CT's come rushing at me. I run back to the middle, and see MORE CT's. I run into the tunnels in hopes that they all rush me like a bunch of lemmings. Well, I got what I wanted. I went up the stairs and chucked a flashbang at my feet just in time to see it go off when all six guys were up the stairs and shooting at me. With everyone blind, I start moving around the map in my head, and leave towards B. I drop a smoke, and wait a few seconds for the footsteps. They throw a flash at me, so I take a few shots with my D.Eagle and run away again, but I nailed a guy on his way out. Grabbed the P90 and ran after tossing my frag grenade in. 5v1.

I weave around the map, from B to CT spawn to where my team died. I grab the bomb, head near T spawn, back through the mid, back through tunnels, and back to B. Peek my head out, nobody's home, and I plant. I immediately switch to my flashbang and wait. Then, the footsteps. Some from the tunnel, some from the door. I chuck it out the door, and when it blows, I run out and kill two guys, taking their equipment. 3v1.

The CT's are at B and the bomb is still ticking. Two guys rush me at the same time I throw a newfound flashbang, and it bounces off of his head, and blinds the three of us. I start spraying my gun in small circles, and sure enough, nailed 'em both. 1v1.

...

The bomb.

I immediately chuck a grenade through the hole in the wall (high part of the wall, just under the marker at B on the map).

Clink-clink.

Clink.

Boom.

Terrorists win.

When my team respawns, everyone flips out about how they lost their money by betting on CT (the in-game, money, of course), and how close the other guy was to defusing the bomb, and how the grenade just bounced off of his head after hitting the walls, then blew up in his face.

Ish happens.

#13937 1 2007-02-08T14:28:43Z TornadoTK
Quadradius is a turn based board game similar to Checkers. You move your pieces around the board, one square a time, trying to jump on (not over) your opponents pieces. However, this is where the similarities end.

Power-ups spawn on the board, and completely devastate your pieces, your opponents pieces, and the game board. It's like Chess, if Chess had random items. Strategy is involved, and you must be prepared for any random event to happen.

Give it a shot, it's actually really fun.
#295874 20 2007-02-10T17:58:03Z TornadoTK
Not putting any limits is like saying, "Hey, here's a free game. Pay if you feel like it." If every game had demos like Soldat did, I'd have a lot of games I'd never pay for.

A demo that has a time-limit is always a bad idea. People hate it when they can only play a game for so long, or when they get kicked out of a game while taking their sweet time through it. Also, "Wait X seconds to continue" screens piss me off. If anything, it should be a simple screen where you have to click an OK button. It involves enough interaction to keep playing while noticing the "Pay Up" message. You could have a "Wait X Seconds" screen between parts of the game where action cools down, such as the end of an episode in N.

A level-limit demo is perfect for Robotology if the level setup is a tad bit similar to N's. 5%-10% of the first part of the game is unlocked for demo play, and a very small pick or two from the middle levels is given. If N had a demo, episodes 00 to 04/09 would be unlocked, and two episodes in the Column 3-7 range would be open. After beating a level, you get the "Pay Up" screen. After an episode, you get the "Wait X Seconds" screen. Certain features should be locked, too. Personal highscores are fine, but uploading them should be locked. Etc. Etc. Etc.

What I'm worried about is security. I've seen small games like Eets, Amradillo Run, and Soldat leaked as a full version online. How will Robotology avoid this?

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
1. Do you think citizens should have the rights to criticize elected officials like the president, governor, or city officials?
Definitely. Just because they have a spiffy position in how our country works doesn't mean they're protected from insults, criticism, and other forms of badmouthing. Our Government runs on being able to vote down a president that we dislike. Voting against them clearly means that you don't want them to be our nation's leader. That is criticism.

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
2. Do you think burning the American flag in anger or protest is an acceptable form of free speech or do you see it as an unacceptable act?
I see it as an acceptable form. Just because it's a bit destructive, it's very symbolic when people from within the nation that once gave a damn about this country do it. When people do it out of hate, well, I can buy their country's flag and burn it, and accomplish the same amount of nothing that they did.

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
3. Do you think religious beliefs that people hold sacred should be open to comedy, criticism, or insults?
Yes, though I am a little shaky when it comes down to insults. Still, I can make fun of your shoes, and you'll still wear them. If I make fun of your religion, you'll still believe in it, right? Anything hateful, on the other hand, is wrong. You can say it, but if you're intentionally pissing someone off, that's crossing the line.

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
4. Do you think books that contain harsh language or controversial subject matter (sexual references, fantasy/witch craft, violence, etc...) should be banned from school libraries?
Only to the younger crowd. A lot of good books wouldn't have shown up in my schools if this was in place. Just because it's controversial doesn't mean it is forbidden. This would give kids the wrong idea, and keeps them from expanding their knowledge with the said books.

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
5. Do you think that speakers or groups, whose views may be unpopular or hateful should be allowed to speak their mind?
Unfortunately, yes. As long as they aren't openly oppressing a specific group of people within the group they are talking about, they can say whatever the hell they want.

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
6. Would you support limiting the jokes people can tell if it would help to decrease insensitive comments about racism, sexism, and intolerance (No ethnic jokes, blonde jokes, jokes about lifestyles, disabilities, etc...) ?
Not really. Just because we make jokes about a group of people, doesn't mean the joke is true. The people who get mad about that are just letting it get to them. I'm not exactly the fittest person on the planet, but even I tell the occasional fat joke. No matter what your situation is, you have to be able to let it go at one point. However, when it comes to actual problems (such as disabilities, medical conditions, etc.), it's not as easy to crack a joke about it without pissing people off in the process. If you do, all you can really do is apologize and look like an ass.

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
7. Do you think that singers/bands should be prevented from writing or performing songs that have profanity or other controversial lyrics in them?
No. If it can be put into a book, a newspaper article, a television show, a blog rant, on a forum, put into poetry, or recreated in any sort of media and still be heard by the people, then music is NO exception.

Quote: firestorm, 2007-07-01T13:13:40Z
8. Should the internet be regulated so that dangerous, obscene, hateful, pornographic, etc... websites would not be permitted?
Dangerous? Maybe sites that are dangerous to your computer. The rest? Hell no. If everything on the internet were to be regulated, what would we do? Knowing your freedoms are not protected online would just drive people away from it in the first place. A lot of the websites we go to would not be the same, possibly even nonexistent. Also, places such as Conservapedia would have to go down as well, and I'm guessing they wouldn't be too pleased about that.

#17163 1 2007-09-10T01:43:59Z TornadoTK
Found this at another set of forums, and I figure it was hilarious enough to spread the word. Even if you don't wanna do it, it's worth the read. I think I might do it, but it falls on a Saturday. (Not a Friday! Whoops!)
Quote
"Pretend to be a Time Traveler" Day

You must spend the entire day in costume and character. The only rule is that you cannot actually tell anyone that you are a time traveler. Other than that, anything's game. There are three possible options:

1) Utopian/clich Future - "If the Future did a documentary of the last fifty years, this is how badly the reenactors would dress." Think Star Trek: TNG or the Time Travelers from Hob. Ever see how the society in Futurama sees the 20th century? Run with it. Your job is to dress with moderately anachronistic clothing and speak in slang from varying decades. Here are some good starters:

- Greet people by referring to things that don't yet exist or haven't existed for a long time. Example: "Have you penetrated the atmosphere lately?" "What spectrum will today's broadcast be in?" and "Your king must be a kindly soul!"
- Show extreme ignorance in operating regular technology. Pay phones should be a complete mystery (try placing the receiver in odd places). Chuckle knowingly at cell phones.

2) Dystopian Future - This one offers a little more flexibility. It can be any kind of future from Terminator to Freejack. The important thing to remember is dress like a crazy person with armor. Black spray painted football pads, high tech visors, torn up trenchcoats and maybe even some dirt here or there. Remember, dystopian future travelers are very startled that they've gone back in time. Some starters:

- If you go the "prisoner who's escaped the future" try shaving your head and putting a barcode on the back of your neck. Then stagger around and stare at the sky, as if you've never seen it before.
- Walk up to random people and say "WHAT YEAR IS THIS?" and when they tell you, get quiet and then say "Then there's still time!" and run off.
- Stand in front of a statue (any statue, really), fall to your knees, and yell "NOOOOOOOOO"
- Stare at newspaper headlines and look astonished.
- Take some trinket with you (it can be anything really), hand it to some stranger, along with a phone number and say "In thirty years dial this number. You'll know what to do after that." Then slip away.

3) The Past - This one is more for beginners. Basically dress in period clothing (preferably Victorian era) and stagger around amazed at everything. Since the culture's set in place already, you have more of a template to work off of. Some pointers:

- Airplanes are terrifying. Also, carry on conversations with televisions for a while.
- Discover and become obsessed with one trivial aspect of technology, like automatic grocery doors. Stay there for hours playing with it.
- Be generally terrified of people who are dressed immodestly compared to your era. Tattoos and shorts on women are especially scary.

And that's it. Remember, the only real rule is staying in character and try to fit in. Never directly admit you're a time traveler, and make really, really bad attempts at keeping a low profile. Naturally, the dystopian future has a little more leeway. And for the record, I've already tried out all of these in real life, in costume. It is so much fun you want to pee yourself.

If anyone has played an online riddler such as God Tower, notpr0n, or especially Dumb: The Game, you'll find these riddles to be (somewhat of) a daunting task. I assure you, I don't intend these riddles to be incredibly hard, but not always will your own knowledge be enough to solve. Get together and put your own analysis' to find the correct answer.

RULES:
- Any discussion of the riddle is permitted.
- Hints will be distributed over time.
- First person to PM the answer and explanation gets the credit. The answer and explanation are to be judged by myself, and as long as you stay within reasonable distance of the answer and theory, you won't be rejected.
- In the event of a team entry, send a single PM naming all involved in the solution.
- If I drop a big hint in IRC, I'll post here. Otherwise, it'll only spread by word-of-mouth.

TIPS:
- Think too small, and you'll miss a clue. Think too big, and you'll catch yourself a red herring. Take breaks while doing a puzzle to get fresh views on what you're doing.
- The title is ALWAYS a hint. It could be one word. It could be the whole thing. Hell, there might even be multiple hints. Again, watch out for herrings.

With that said, lets start the show. Good luck to you all!

#412629 9 2008-02-28T03:37:15Z TornadoTK
I gotta agree, this sounds like a horribly large project. What physics engine do you plan on using? What programming language? Do you have people on your team with a vast amount of experience with netcode?

-full interactivity with environments
To address all of the things that you have said, you need one killer physics engine. The guys behind the new Red Faction game have talked about their latest engine, which allows all of the effects you desire, and they talk about it being one hell of an engine to manage. Another issue they had when designing levels using that engine is that buildings had to be structurally sound; if a building wouldn't stand in real life, it wouldn't stand in the game. This required way more additional research.

-realistic bullet flight - bullets are effected by wind and gravity
This isn't so hard, as long as you can code well and you understand ballistic physics.

-realistic damage to personnel and vehicles eg. inhibited movement from being shot in the leg, loss of control of a vehicle from having the tire shot out
-continuous bleeding (you will bleed and leave a trail on the ground if you are wounded)
Both have been done in the past, and they were executed successfully, so this should not be a problem.

-large, expanseful maps - 20-50 people will be able to play on one map without it feeling crowded
This takes a lot of work. With the complexity of the engine/level design/physics mentioned before, designing levels that are this large will be tough to balance out well.

-not requiring a powerful compy to play it well
I don't know how you can pull off all of the above AND have it be friendly with aging computers, but if you can... Wow.


Not trying to kick you in the face, but these are all problems you will have to deal with at one point. Good luck with the project.

#428304 20 2008-04-14T06:19:08Z TornadoTK
Not sure if this applies much to current games (unless you get into organized clans), but a valuable skill I've learned over my years of multiplayer gaming:

Teamwork.

Whether it's giving orders or taking them, so much more gets accomplished (and it gets accomplished more efficiently) when a few people in a group become a real team. You build skills based around communication, organization, decision-making, time and resource management, and most importantly, working in a structured system. Many of these skills are vital in the business world of today.

Games like Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory and the older Rainbow Six titles are excellent examples of team-based strategy, and a solid team makes you an unstoppable force. Many games today have you working as a team (Halo 3, CoD4, Team Fortress 2), but the feeling is a little less enjoyable unless you have friends there with you.

"Like lots of people said, it's got much more difficult guitar parts than on Rock Band."

"The guitar controller in Rock Band is messed up. The bottons stick, the whammy bar is terrible, the extra fret buttons near the bottom of the neck are useless, and the strum bar all around sucks. Yes, I admit, I don't like the clicky buttons (bottons?) but they don't stick for me. "The GHWT drums look awesome, especially compared to the RB2 drums. The RB2 ones look immensely huge and unnessesary."

Quote: Raigan, August 05, 2008 09:16 am
This is definitely nothing specific to N+, my guess is that it's a problem with the XBLA DRM scheme, which apparently is getting fixed in the new dashboard update.

When you buy a game, it gets registered to (1) your physical xbox via its serial number, (2) your gamertag.

To play the full version of a game, it needs to verify that you've bought it via (1) _OR_ (2). (1) requires that you're running it on the xbox you bought it on (not just the HD/memory card AFAIK), (2) requires that you have an internet connection.

Are you sure you didn't have an internet connection the previous times? And/or possibly you need to have your gamertag info on the HD.

Basically, I don't know

But the stupid DRM stuff is definitely annoying, NONE of our games work if our internet goes out, because we've had RRoD twice and thus verification method (1) no longer works..

http://www.xbox.com/en-US/support/systemus...censemigration/

Transfer your DRM's to your current console. It's not exactly the greatest method, but it works for now, and is way easier than the previous process (complain to customer support until they stop passing you around the small people and give you to an executive).
